tasks.title: Review the 42 object labels
tasks.body: Apply the caption checklist, then ask Prism to review the twelve most complex labels.

tasks.title: Verify the step-free visitor route
tasks.body: Check entrance width, turning space and the route to every gallery. Attach the review notes.

tasks.title: Approve the Gallery C lighting study
tasks.body: Compare the two lighting layouts. Keep the conservation limit visible in the decision record.

tasks.title: Rehearse three guided routes
tasks.body: Run the family, discovery and quiet-preview routes. Record the actual duration of each rehearsal.

tasks.title: Prepare the multilingual sign set
tasks.body: Use the approved room names and add the large-print visitor map.

tasks.title: Resolve the Gallery B capacity change
tasks.body: Replace the older capacity claim only after the new floor plan has been independently reviewed.

tasks.title: Publish the installation timetable
tasks.body: Separate placement, safety checks and guide rehearsal. Include a named owner for each block.

tasks.title: Proofread the exhibition catalogue
tasks.body: Check object titles, section headings and references against the final caption register.

tasks.title: Prepare accessible audio descriptions
tasks.body: Draft descriptions for twelve focal objects. Review clarity before recording any narration.

tasks.title: Schedule the quiet preview
tasks.body: Reserve a low-noise opening hour and brief the visitor team on the agreed route.

decisions.title: Offer a quiet preview before opening night
decisions.body: Open the galleries one hour early for visitors who prefer a quieter experience.

decisions.title: Choose the low-glare Gallery C layout
decisions.body: Prefer the low-glare layout if the conservation and readability checks both pass.

decisions.title: Increase Gallery B entrance slots
decisions.body: Use the revised 96-person capacity after the floor plan receives an independent check.

## Opening night: the next three priorities
**Atlas:** check the visitor route. **Scribe:** finish the caption review. **Prism:** prepare the lighting comparison.
Keep each result with its evidence; proposals still need approval.

### Visitor route review
The step-free route reaches all **six galleries**. Two signs need larger text.
- East entrance: clear
- Gallery C turning space: checked
- Quiet-preview route: ready for a second review

The caption register now contains **42 object labels**. Twelve complex labels are flagged for Prism.
The first review reduced the average length from 112 to 68 words. I recorded both the outcome and the remaining work in Knowledge.

I compared the two lighting layouts. The **low-glare option** is easier to read, but the conservation check is still pending.
I have kept the lighting task blocked rather than marking it complete.

**Approved:** keep the quiet preview and the common caption format.
**Still open:** Gallery B capacity and the lighting check. Please use the decision register before changing either plan.

**Fictional museum demo** · The installation timetable is ready. ✅
Atlas and Scribe have received the handover. Prism will verify the final sign set next.
**Today’s check:** reconcile the brief, source dates and open tasks before the next shift.

current.body:
# Exhibition collaboration rules

## 1. Keep the work visible
Every task has one owner, a concrete next step and a due date when needed. Record the result and its evidence.

## 2. Separate proposals from permission
Agents propose changes. The Curator approves them. Approval does not execute a change; the owner records implementation afterwards.

## 3. Verify independently
The person who implements a safety or accessibility change cannot also verify it. Keep the reviewer’s evidence with the decision.

## 4. Read the current sources
Use the latest exhibition brief, accessibility review and installation plan. A stale note remains history until its source has been checked.

## 5. Preserve the next shift’s context
Record what worked, what failed and what is still open. Complete the daily knowledge check before handing over.

All information in this museum example is fictional. No real people, organisations or operational records are represented.
